steps: Atomic number was chosen to arrange the elements because the physical and chemical properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers.
When elements are arranged in increasing order of atomic number, elements with similar properties occur at regular intervals.
This arrangement also places isotopes of an element in the same position, because they have the same atomic number.
items.finalAnswer: The properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers, so atomic number gives the correct basis for arranging the periodic table.

steps: The word “periodic” means that something repeats at regular intervals.
In the periodic table, the properties of elements repeat at regular intervals when elements are arranged in order of increasing atomic number.
items.finalAnswer: “Periodic” means that the properties of elements repeat at regular intervals.

steps: The size of a period depends on the number of electrons accommodated in the shells being filled.
As we move down the periodic table, new shells have greater capacity to accommodate electrons.
Therefore, more elements are needed to fill these shells and the size of the periods increases.
items.finalAnswer: Periods become larger down the table because the shells being filled can accommodate more electrons.

steps: The elements in a group have the same number of electrons in their outermost shell because their atoms have similar outer electronic configurations.
As we move down a group, new electron shells are added, but the number of electrons in the outermost shell remains the same.
items.finalAnswer: Elements in the same group have the same number of outermost-shell electrons because their outer electronic configurations are similar.

Sodium has one electron in its outermost shell and can lose it more readily than calcium can lose its two outermost electrons.
Therefore, sodium is more reactive than calcium.
items.finalAnswer: No. Sodium is more reactive because it loses its outermost electron more readily than calcium loses its electrons.

steps: Atomic radius generally decreases from left to right across a period because nuclear charge increases and pulls the electrons closer to the nucleus.
In the third period, sodium has the maximum atomic radius and argon has the minimum atomic radius.
items.finalAnswer: Sodium has the maximum atomic radius and argon has the minimum atomic radius in the third period.

steps: Elements in the sixth and seventh groups have six and seven electrons, respectively, in their outermost shells.
They need only two or one electrons, respectively, to complete their outermost shell.
Therefore, they attract electrons strongly and have high electronegativity.
items.finalAnswer: Elements in the sixth and seventh groups are highly electronegative because they need only two or one electrons to complete their outermost shells.

steps: The first ionization energy removes an electron from a neutral magnesium atom.
After losing one electron, magnesium becomes a positively charged ion, Mg⁺.
The remaining electrons are attracted more strongly by the positively charged ion, so more energy is required to remove the second electron.
items.finalAnswer: The second ionization energy of magnesium is greater because the second electron is removed from the positively charged Mg⁺ ion.
